Aaron Judge is an outfielder and one of the Yankees' current superstars, known for his towering home runs and imposing physical presence at six feet seven inches tall. His two thousand twenty-two season, in which he hit sixty-two home runs to break the American League single-season record, revitalized Yankees fandom and cemented his place in the franchise's storied lineage.

In two thousand twenty-two, Judge hit sixty-two home runs, breaking Roger Maris' American League single-season record set in nineteen sixty-one and captivating the nation. He has averaged over forty home runs per season as a Yankee, establishing himself as one of the most prolific sluggers of his generation. That same year, Judge won the American League MVP award and was voted captain of the Yankees in two thousand twenty-three, a rare honor for a player in his prime. He is the tallest player in Major League Baseball at six feet seven inches, which gives his home runs a distinctive arc and enables a wider strike zone. Judge has become the face of the Yankees and has drawn comparisons to Babe Ruth and Mickey Mantle for his power and home-run appeal. He remains a key figure in the Yankees' quest to win their first World Series since two thousand nine. Alex Rodriguez, a former Yankees superstar, has a power-hitting legacy that Judge carries forward, following in the footsteps of Derek Jeter, the legendary captain and franchise legend.
